history.description: After a pioneer named Lewis sold his property, Dr. Davenport helped establish a post office at his home, which served as the foundation for the town of Xenia.
The construction of the railroad through the area provided a significant boost to the local economy and helped expand the village's footprint.
By 1870, Xenia had grown significantly, reaching a population of approximately 1,000 residents.
The village held a major celebration to commemorate its 150th anniversary.
As of the 2020 Census, Xenia remains a small, historic village in Clay County with a population of 380 residents.
